sources: https://www.blm.gov/visit/rocky-point-east (read 2026-11-26): 'Rocky Point Campground is located on the north shore of Eagle Lake outside of Susanville, CA. This is a small undeveloped campground on the east shore of Rocky Point. The site is best suited for self-contained camping. There is no potable water or trash removal available but a vault toilet is provided.' 'The surface in the campground is packed earth, gravel or sand. It is possible to launch small boats along the shoreline in the campground area.' Directions: 'follow the unimproved dirt road south 1.25 miles along the shoreline until you reach a broad gravel flat which is the unimproved camping area where there are two vault toilets and a bulletin board.' Fees: 'Camping and day use are free; donations are appreciated.' Stay Limit: 'Overnight camping is allowed for 14-consecutive days within a 28-day period.' Contact: Eagle Lake Field Office '530-252-5303'
https://www.blm.gov/visit/eagle-lake (read 2026-11-26): 'Eagle Lake is a closed basin lake with its water levels fluctuating with variations of inflow.'

note: Undeveloped BLM camping area on a gravel flat at the east shore of Rocky Point, on the north end of Eagle Lake. Reached by 1.25 mi of unimproved dirt road along the shore from the Bucks Bay subdivision off County Rd A1; there are no marked sites and campers park on packed earth, gravel or sand beside the water. Small boats can be launched from the shore; at low water only from firm gravel at the far end of the point. Self-contained camping; no trash service. --Claude
summary: Rocky Point - East (BLM, Eagle Lake): lakefront kept (open gravel flat at the water, no trees); free, 14-day limit, two vault toilets, no water; note corrected ('west shore' -> east shore of Rocky Point); phone and website changes flagged.
flags: WATERFRONT lakefront KEPT (not --AWH). No numbered sites - an undeveloped open flat, free, first come. Esri imagery (40.6730,-120.7432, 300 m frame) shows the treeless gravel/earth flat at the stored pin running to within ~10-50 m of the lake edge over open ground, with only a ~10 m band of low shore vegetation; BLM: 'It is possible to launch small boats along the shoreline in the campground area.' Pads are flat and barely above the water, so the kayak test passes. Eagle Lake is a natural closed-basin lake ('water levels fluctuating'), so there is no dam full pool; the flat is the shore at any recent level. Proposed evidence: 'BLM page 2026-11-26 (boats launch along the shoreline in the campground area) + Esri imagery 40.6730,-120.7432: open gravel flat within ~10-50 m of the water, no trees.'

PIN: stored 40.67340,-120.74500 is on the camping flat - keep. BLM's listed coordinate 40.67589,-120.744274 (~290 m N) is generic (the same coordinate appears on the Rocky Point West page) and falls on grass north of the flat.
